__doc__: Repo-local maw config layer — ENGINE+MODEL ALIASES for teams spawned from this repo.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS:
`maw team up` forwards ONLY `-e <engine-name>` to `maw wake`. It never forwards
a model. `maw wake` has no --model flag at all. So the ONLY place a model can be
expressed is inside the command string of a registered engine alias — right here.
A charter's `model:` field is parsed and validated by maw, then never read.
See psi/teams/ENGINE-AND-MODEL.md for the full evidence.
HOW IT IS PICKED UP [verified 2026-08-06 on maw-rs 325db65]:
maw walks up from cwd collecting every <ancestor>/.maw/maw.config.<N>.json layer
(crates/maw-xdg/src/config.rs :: discover_config_layers + parse_config_layer_name)
and deep-merges them, sorted by N ascending. Global lives at
~/.config/maw/maw.config.50.json (N=50), so N=60 here merges AFTER it and wins.
The filename MUST match maw.config.<digits>.json — any other name is ignored
silently, including a plain maw.config.json with no digits.
Proof: with only a `probe-engine-xyz` key in this file,
maw wake codex-fanout --no-attach --dry-run -e probe-engine-xyz
-> command: MAW_SESSION_WINDOW=codex-fanout echo PROBE-ENGINE-XYZ-RESOLVED
RULES FOR EDITING:
1. ADD namespaced keys only. Never redefine `default`, `codex`, `claude`,
`thclaws`, or any *-oracle key — this layer outranks global for every maw
command run anywhere inside this repo, so a redefinition here silently
changes behaviour for unrelated work in the same tree.
2. After editing, run:  bash psi/teams/scripts/verify-check.sh enginecheck <charter>
An alias that is not registered does NOT fail loudly — it falls through to the
window name, then a glob, then `default`. You get a working engine that is not
the one you asked for. That is the whole reason this file and that check exist.
3. Keep paths PATH-relative (`codex`, not /home/user/...). This repo's charters
and skills must survive a path move and an owner handoff.

These two names were NOT two versions of one alias. They were two DIFFERENT aliases
that collided: ours meant MODEL TIER (gpt-5.6 vs -mini, effort untouched); loom's and
lucifer's meant REASONING EFFORT on the default model. Same name, different dimension,
so `which version wins` had no answer. [verified 2026-08-07: lucifer's v9-canary charter

We renamed OURS because ours had 2 call sites and theirs had ~57 charters. That frees
the bare names to mean effort everywhere, and their charters need zero edits.
Why it mattered: moving the effort meaning to user-level would have booted 57 charters
SUCCESSFULLY on the wrong dimension — exit 0, no warning, and REGISTERED, so enginecheck
and enginereg both pass. Visible at the status bar only. Silent-wrong beats null, badly.
